profile.summary: PAGTN, the path-augmented graph transformer network, is a graph neural network for molecular property prediction. Instead of only aggregating from immediate neighbours, it computes features of the paths between pairs of atoms and uses them to build global attention layers, so that distant parts of a molecule can influence each other directly. The authors trained it on quantum chemistry, physical chemistry and biochemistry property datasets; the name appears on this benchmark database because the DeepProtein benchmark trained it as a baseline on protein tasks.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The authors' starting point is that graph convolution networks rely on local aggregation and so can miss higher-order graph properties. The repository precomputes shortest paths in the molecular graph as a preprocessing step, and the paper uses path features in molecular graphs to build global attention layers. The repository's training script exposes the path length as a flag, with a maximum path length of 3 in the published command, along with position and ring embeddings, a hidden size of 160 and two attention heads. In the DeepProtein configuration the model is five PAGTN layers with LeakyReLU activation and node embedding dimension 64.

sections.title: Use as a benchmark baseline
sections.body: The DeepProtein benchmark did not use the authors' repository. Its PAGTN encoder imports PAGTNGNN from the dgllife library and adds a weighted sum and max readout and a linear layer to the predictor dimension. The benchmark groups PAGTN with the graph transformers it added because, it says, graph transformers have recently shown their power in protein function prediction. A protein result against the name PAGTN is therefore a dgllife path-augmented network the benchmark trained, not a checkpoint from the authors.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository has no releases, no version number and no trained weights: it ships the model code, the preprocessing script, the training script and the data and splits used in the paper as data.zip, plus the scripts that generated the published results. A result must therefore name the commit and the training flags used; this page read commit 4fd3606d49e81ebbe009aa9c69add16bd092d4d1. The README also gives two other model types behind the same script, a local variant selected with -mask_neigh and a convolutional network selected with -model_type conv_net, so a result must say which was run. For a protein result, name the benchmark library instead; the DeepProtein README says its legacy graph encoders, PAGTN among them, are not available in its version 2 runtime.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Graph transformer for molecular property prediction, trained per task. Not a pretrained protein model.

quotes.text: we propose Path-Augmented Graph Transformer Networks (PAGTN) that are explicitly built on longer-range dependencies in graph-structured data

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Global attention layers built from path features in the molecular graph, after a shortest-path preprocessing step, with optional position and ring embeddings. The published command uses hidden size 160, two attention heads, maximum path length 3 and ten rounds; the DeepProtein configuration uses five PAGTN layers with node embedding dimension 64.

-model_type transformer -hidden_size 160 \
-no_share -n_heads 2 -d_k 80 -dropout 0.2
The model consists of 5 PAGTN layers with LeakyReLU activation. Node embedding dimension is 64.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A molecular graph with its shortest paths precomputed by preprocess/shortest_paths.py over a data directory. In the protein benchmark the graph is built from the sequence by way of a SMILES string, with edge features added by an edge featuriser.

It generally transforms the input sequence into a valid SMILES string, then transforms the chemical substance into a graph.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A graph-level property prediction for the trained task; the published command trains with a mean squared error loss. In the benchmark encoder the pooled features go through a linear layer to the predictor dimension.

strengths.text: Path features give every pair of atoms a direct attention link, which the authors propose as a fix for the local aggregation of graph convolution networks.

quotes.text: These models rely on local aggregation operations and can therefore miss higher-order graph properties. To remedy this, we propose Path-Augmented Graph Transformer Networks (PAGTN)

strengths.text: The repository ships the paper's data and splits and the scripts that produced the published results, so an experiment can be repeated without rebuilding the datasets.

strengths.text: The authors report that PAGTN consistently beat graph convolution networks on the property datasets they tested, which is their own comparison.

quotes.text: We compare our PAGTN model against the GCN model and show that our model consistently outperforms GCNs on molecular property prediction datasets

run_guide.summary: Set up the authors' conda environment, compute the shortest paths for a dataset and train the path-augmented transformer on it.
prerequisites: Conda, with the rdkit channel available.
A CUDA 10.0 GPU machine for the -cuda flag in the training command.
A dataset directory; the repository ships the paper's data and splits in data.zip.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/benatorc/PA-Graph-Transformer.git
cd PA-Graph-Transformer
git checkout --detach 4fd3606d49e81ebbe009aa9c69add16bd092d4d1
steps.explanation: The README gives no clone command, so the clone and the checkout of the commit this page read were added here. The remaining steps are copied from the README.

quotes.text: This is the github repo for the paper "Path-Augmented Graph Transformer Network"

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
conda create -c rdkit -n prop_predictor rdkit
source activate prop_predictor
conda install pytorch torchvision cudatoolkit=10.0 -c pytorch
conda install scikit-learn tqdm
steps.explanation: The four commands the README gives for its conda environment, in order. The README notes the set up can differ slightly by system.

steps.title: Put the repository on the Python path
steps.explanation: Taken from the README as printed; replace path_to_repo with the checkout directory.

quotes.text: export PYTHONPATH=path_to_repo:

steps.title: Compute the shortest paths
steps.explanation: The preprocessing step that produces the path features the model attends over. Replace path_to_data with the dataset directory, for example one unpacked from data.zip.

quotes.text: To compute the shortest paths, run the following:
python preprocess/shortest_paths.py -data_dir path_to_data

steps.title: Train the path-augmented transformer
steps.shell:
dataset=path_to_dataset
python train/train_prop.py -cuda \
    -data $dataset -loss_type mse \
    -max_grad_norm 10 -batch_size 50 -num_epochs 100 \
	-output_dir output_test/sol_transformer -n_rounds 10 \
	-model_type transformer -hidden_size 160 \
	-p_embed -ring_embed -max_path_length 3 -lr 5e-4 \
	-no_share -n_heads 2 -d_k 80 -dropout 0.2
steps.explanation: The README's command for the transformer model, copied as printed, including its tab indentation. Adding -mask_neigh runs the local variant, and -model_type conv_net runs the convolutional network instead.
